title: Shaky Hands, Steady Drops

patient.name: Mdm Lim Guek Eng
patient.presenting_complaint: On daily eye drops but struggles to instil them due to arthritic, shaky hands

history.hpc: Mdm Lim says 'My hand got arthritis, cannot squeeze the bottle and aim, always miss my eye.' She needs her drops instilled and practical advice as her hand dexterity makes self-instillation difficult.
history.pmhx: Arthritis affecting the hands. On daily eye drops. No drug allergies (confirm).
history.social_hx: Lives with her son who could help with drops.

va.right: Not the focus of this station
va.left: Not the focus of this station

examination_findings.anterior_segment: No active infection that would change technique

investigations.task: Instil the charted drop and give practical strategies for a patient with poor hand dexterity
investigations.key_points: Confirm identity, eye, drop and allergy; suggest techniques such as resting the hand on the forehead, lying down, the pocket method, a drop-aid device, or asking a family member to help; ensure she can manage at home

diagnosis: The charted drop is instilled and practical strategies are given for a patient whose arthritis limits self-instillation: stabilising the hand on the forehead, lying down, using the lower-lid pocket, a drop-aid device, or family help. Identity, eye, drop and allergy are confirmed. This is a procedural/teaching station.

immediate: Confirm identity, the correct eye and the charted drop and strength
Check for drug/eye-drop allergy before instilling
Instil one drop into the lower fornix using a no-touch technique
Suggest stabilising strategies: rest the bottle hand on the forehead, lie down, or use the pocket method
Suggest a drop-aid device or family member assistance if needed
Confirm she or a helper can manage the drops at home
Document the drop, eye, time and allergy check
follow_up: Arrange a drop aid or family support if self-instillation remains difficult
Advise reporting if she cannot get the drops in reliably
patient_education: Teach steadying the hand on the forehead and using the lower-lid pocket
Suggest lying down to make aiming easier
Reassure that a drop in the pocket still works and family/aids can help

key_points: Confirms identity, correct eye and the charted drop
Identifies the dexterity difficulty and home support
Instils one drop into the lower fornix (no-touch)
Suggests a drop aid or family help
Recognises poor dexterity as the key barrier
Knows practical aids and techniques to overcome it
Understands the importance of reliable dosing
Documents drop, eye, time and allergy check
